profile.name: Ledgerly Inc.
profile.summary: US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.
businessLines: Prepaid / debit card program via sponsor bank
applies: Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets
doesNotApply: SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

aml-bsa.description: AML/BSA program, FinCEN, Travel Rule, SARs

consumer-payments.description: Reg E, remittances, prepaid, CFPB supervision, UDAAP

prompts.jevQuestion: Would the general counsel of this company need to know about this federal document because it could create, change or remove a compliance obligation or material legal risk for the company's actual business lines? Routine filings for other industries are not relevant.
prompts.extractSystem: Extract every dated obligation or deadline (comment due, effective, compliance) stated in the text. Quote the sentence verbatim. If none, return an empty list.
prompts.actionsSystem: Write one action item per document for a busy general counsel: an imperative sentence (≤ 25 words) saying what the owner should do and why, in plain English a non-lawyer understands — spell out acronyms, no regulatory jargon. Do NOT write any dates or citations — those are rendered separately from verified data.
prompts.webLeadsSystem: You find leads on new US federal regulatory actions. Search, then list the URLs you found. Do not summarise law from memory.
prompts.webLeadsPrompt:
{{profile}}

Find US federal regulatory developments (final rules, proposed rules, guidance, enforcement) published {{windowStart}} to {{windowEnd}} that could affect this company. Run at most 3 searches. Reply with the URLs only.
prompts.panelJudge:
You are one judge on a panel grading action items that a General Counsel would forward to a colleague.
For EVERY item and EVERY listed criterion, answer PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN (UNKNOWN only if the item gives you too little to decide), with a one-line reason.
Judge only the criterion asked. Do not judge whether the rule is truly relevant to the company — that is graded elsewhere.
Each item is a card as the reader sees it: the action text plus "datesShown" (verified dates displayed next to the action) and "tier". Action texts deliberately contain no dates, so a date the rubric mentions counts as covered when it appears in "datesShown".
For "covers", a paraphrase that conveys the business-relevant substance counts; exact names, populations and sub-details are not required.

Criteria:
{{criteria}}

Items (a "rubric" is present only when the answer key has one for that item):
{{items}}

question: Would the general counsel of this company need to know about this federal document because it could create, change or remove a compliance obligation or material legal risk for the company's actual business lines? Routine filings for other industries are not relevant.
state:
Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
- Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
- FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

[2026-22337] Proposed Rule — Federal Communications Commission
Title: Unleashing the Power of Unlicensed Ultra-Wideband Devices; Petition of Robert Bosch LLC for Amendment of the Part 15 Subpart F Ultra-Wideband Rules; and Petition of Alliance for Automative Innovation et al. To Amend Part 15 of the FCC's Rules To Permit the Operation of Certain Ultra-Wideband Devices
Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: The Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) proposes to update its rules for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) devices to reflect significant technological developments since the rules were first adopted in 2002. UWB technology has matured into a widely used, low-power enabler that supports applications in tracking, automation, precision location, health monitoring, athletic performance, and public safety. As capabilities of UWB have expanded, the existing rules have not kept pace with the technological change, resulting in an increasing number of waiver requests received by the Commission to authorize modern devices. The Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeks comment on revisions intended to modernize the UWB framework, provide greater flexibility for future applications, promote continued innovation, and ensure the protection of incumbent federal and non-federal spectrum users.

[2026-22380] Rule — Health and Human Services Department; Office of the Secretary
Title: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or Department) issues this rule to revise the regulation implementing section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (section 504) as it applies to recipients of HHS funding (entitled "Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance," ("2024 Final Rule")), published on May 9, 2024. This rule clarifies that the Department interprets the statutory exclusion of "gender identity disorders not resulting from physical impairments" from the terms "individual with a disability" and "disability" set forth in our regulations to encompass "gender dysphoria not resulting from a physical impairment" for purposes of the regulation. This clarification is necessary to resolve ambiguity introduced in the preamble to the 2024 Final Rule and to ensure compliance with the best reading of the governing statute.

[2026-22383] Proposed Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
Action: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
Abstract: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-25-09, which applies to certain The Boeing Company Model 757 airplanes. AD 2024-25-09 requires installing new relays and changing certain wire bundles leading to the power transfer unit (PTU) control valve. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-25-09, the FAA determined that the requirements bulletin mandated by AD 2024-25-09 contains errors. In some cases, those errors prevent the actions required by AD 2024-25-09 from being fully accomplished. In other cases, the errors would allow actions that could introduce new hazards affecting the operation and thus the availability of the PTU. This proposed AD would require, depending on the airplane configuration, installing new relays and new connectors, changing certain wire bundles, doing an operational test, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

[2026-22450] Proposed Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Update and Clarification of the Passenger Facility Charge Regulations
Action: Supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking (SNPRM).
Abstract: On September 27, 2023 FAA published a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) to amend its Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) regulations to implement congressionally mandated changes to an existing pilot program within the PFC program. FAA also proposed to reaffirm existing program requirements and update or remove obsolete references within the PFC regulations. Following publication of the NPRM and before FAA issued a final rule, the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (the 2024 Act) was signed into law on May 16, 2024. Several sections of the 2024 Act necessitate changes to PFC regulations or modifications to proposals made in the NPRM. As such, FAA now issues this supplemental proposal addressing: PFC turnback reductions; two new PFC-eligible projects; restrictions to PFC-eligible projects; FAA's timeline for review and acknowledgement of notice of intent (NOI) submissions; PFC streamlining review eligibility; and PFC submittal requirements. This proposal aligns with the requirements established by the 2024 Act.

That action was considered an interim action. Since the FAA issued AD 2025- 20-02, updated software has been developed and instructions have been issued for installing the software. In addition, revised operational instructions have been issued that are applicable after installation of the updated software. This proposed AD would require installing the updated software and incorporating the applicable revised operational instructions into the AFM. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

[2026-22576] Rule — Environmental Protection Agency
Title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (25-3.5e)
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: EPA is issuing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNURs require persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any of these chemical substances for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification; made an appropriate determination regarding that notification; and taken such actions as required by that determination.

[2026-22649] Rule — Legal Services Corporation
Title: Cost Standards and Procedures; Purchasing and Property Management
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: This final rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC or Corporation) regulations governing cost allowability, prior approval requirements, and property and procurement standards applicable to LSC recipients. The final rule clarifies when recipients must obtain prior approval for expenditures of LSC funds; increases the monetary threshold for prior approval; clarifies the treatment of proceeds from fundraising activities supported with LSC funds; provides additional flexibility in LSC's review of prior approval requests; clarifies documentation requirements for prior approval requests; and revises the deadline and requirements for accounting for LSC funds invested in real estate. These amendments are intended to clarify existing requirements, reduce administrative burden, promote consistent oversight and enforcement, and strengthen accountability in the use of Federal funds.

[2026-22717] Rule — Justice Department; Drug Enforcement Administration
Title: Specific Listing for 3-Chloromethcathinone, A Currently Controlled Schedule I Substance
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is establishing a specific listing and DEA Controlled Substances Code Number (drug code) for 1-(3-chlorophenyl)-2-(methylamino)propan-1-one (3- chloromethcathinone; 3-CMC) in schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). Although 3-chloromethcathinone is not specifically listed in schedule I of the CSA with its own unique drug code, it is a schedule I controlled substances in the United States because it is a positional isomer of 4-chloromethcathinone, which is a schedule I hallucinogen. Therefore, DEA is simply amending the schedule I hallucinogenic substances list in its regulations to separately include 3- chloromethcathinone.
